overview: Render pending messages under a stable clientMessageId and reconcile the server acknowledgement into the same row. Apply sequence-ordered events, dedup retries and backfill gaps after reconnect. Auto-scroll only if the reader was already near the bottom. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.assumption: 20 incoming events/s; render batches every 100 ms as an illustrative target
estimation.calculation: At most ~10 event-driven render batches/s rather than 20 separate commits
estimation.result: Batching limits churn but adds up to ~100 ms presentation delay
estimation.implication: Measure interaction latency and ensure input updates stay immediate; presence can tolerate more coalescing.

components.purpose: Keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive-technology entry point. Client architecture only; backend internals are external dependencies.
components.rationale: Own this responsibility at the Browser / User boundary; keep communication explicit through the diagrammed dependency.

components.purpose: Render pending messages under a stable clientMessageId and reconcile the server acknowledgement into the same row. Apply sequence-ordered events, dedup retries and backfill gaps after reconnect. Auto-scroll only if the reader was already near the bottom. Performance plan: 50 messages per page; many conversations but only one active visible timeline; batch incoming events and bound DOM/history. Accessibility: Label composer and send button, keep keyboard focus while sending, announce relevant new messages politely without rereading history; do not force scroll while the user is reading older content. Failure recovery: Dedup by ID, detect sequence gap and fetch missing range; retry a failed send with its original clientMessageId. Subscription cleanup prevents cross-room leakage. Trade-off: Polling is simpler for low-frequency messaging. WebSocket lowers latency but requires backfill, connection lifecycle and multi-tab policy.

steps.title: Capture user intent without duplicating authority
steps.explanation: Validate local input and enter a pending state. Use the component callback rather than mutating server snapshots directly.

steps.title: Send the versioned operation
steps.explanation: Call POST /conversations/{id}/messages through the API adapter. Request: {clientMessageId:"local1",body:"Hi"}. A prior successful response or unresolved operation must not be overwritten by a stale retry.

steps.title: Reconcile or expose recovery
steps.explanation: Dedup by ID, detect sequence gap and fetch missing range; retry a failed send with its original clientMessageId. Subscription cleanup prevents cross-room leakage. Update the query key with the acknowledged version or invalidate/refetch it; maintain focus and make pending/error state visible.

failureCases.scenario: Socket reconnect delivers a duplicate and skips an event
failureCases.handling: Dedup by ID, detect sequence gap and fetch missing range; retry a failed send with its original clientMessageId. Subscription cleanup prevents cross-room leakage.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
